Six classic valve amps, each drawn as a playable panel. Pick any two, set one, and translate the setting to the other; put pedals in front from the pedalboard below. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Learn the blocks inside a valve amp: preamp valves, tone stack, power valves, rectifier, cabinet.
2. Hear two amps side by side and translate a setting from one to the other.
3. Put pedals in front of the amp and hear how the amp changes them.
:::

## What the circuits do

- **Preamp valves** (12AX7 / ECC83 triodes) amplify the guitar many times. Pushed hard they clip, more on one side than the other, which adds even harmonics. More stages in a row, **cascaded**, give more gain: the Mesa/Boogie's idea (Wikipedia, "Mesa Boogie").
- The **tone stack** is a passive network of three pots, three capacitors and a resistor: it can only cut (Wikipedia, "Tone stack"). The Fender Bassman 5F6-A made the three-knob Treble / Middle / Bass stack the standard (Wikipedia). This page computes each stack's curve **exactly from its component values**, with the closed formula of Yeh and Smith (2006), and the test checks that formula against a separate circuit solve.
- On a Fender Twin the stack comes right after the first valve; on the Bassman and the Marshall it comes after the second valve and a cathode follower; the Vox Top Boost is the Bassman stack **with the middle control removed** (Wikipedia, "Vox AC30").
- The **power valves** work in a **push-pull** pair: one handles the top half of the wave, one the bottom, so even harmonics cancel. Biased hot (towards class A) they are smoother; the AC30 is class AB, cathode biased and without negative feedback (Wikipedia, "Vox AC30").
- The **rectifier** turns mains AC into the valves' high voltage. A valve rectifier (GZ34: the Bassman, the AC30) **sags** on loud notes, so the amp compresses; solid state (the Twin) barely does (Wikipedia, "Fender Twin Reverb").
- The **cabinet** shapes the sound most of all: open-back 2x12s and 4x10s, closed 4x12s, a bass 8x10. Here each is a filter that stands in for a speaker's response (the site's curves, not measured).

## Two amps side by side

Choose an amp for each side. Drag a knob (arrow keys work too), click a switch, press a ▶ button. The instrument is the site's pickup model ([Electric Guitars Compared](guitar-compare.qmd), [Electric Basses Compared](bass-compare.qmd)); **Pedals in front** puts a pedal model before the amp, or the pedalboard further down this page. The graph is the tone controls and cabinet (the valves' distortion is left out). The ☀ / ☾ button switches every panel between a white and a black background.

```{=html}
<div class="ampc" data-a="twin" data-b="ac30"></div>
```

## Translating between amps

**Translate** finds the setting on the other amp that sounds most like this one, in two steps:

1. **Drive**: a test chord goes through both amps (preamp and power, no cabinet) at two levels 12 dB apart. A clean amp's output changes by 12 dB; a driven one by less. The other amp's gain knobs are set so the change matches.
2. **Tone**: the tone stack, bright switch, Presence or Cut and the cabinet are compared as curves from 80 Hz to 8 kHz; the other amp's tone knobs are set to the closest curve.

The report says **exact** (almost the same numbers), **approx** (the closest setting, with what is lost: reverb, tremolo, a missing Middle knob, the Cut) or **lost** (nothing close). Try the Twin into the AC30, the Bassman into the Plexi (the same circuit, other values), or the Plexi flat out into the Twin.

## Pedals in front

Set **Pedals in front** above to "The pedalboard on this page" and the chain below goes before the amp. Drag the pedals to reorder them.

```{=html}
<div class="pdb" data-chain="ts808,dm2"></div>
```

Things to try: a Tube Screamer in front of the Plexi at crunch (the mids push the amp harder); a Fuzz Face in front of the Twin (the clean amp lets the fuzz through as it is); a delay in front of a driven amp (the repeats distort together) and in front of a clean one.

## What is this site's own

- Only the tone-stack formula and the Bassman's component values are from a source read in full (Yeh and Smith). The other amps' stack values are the commonly published schematic values, from memory: unverified. Stage gains, bias, sag, reverb, tremolo, Cut range, the SVT's tone section and the Rectifier's switches are the site's (marked in `apps/shared/lessons/amps.js`).
- The panels are drawn after photos, not measured drawings; no makers' logos; the panel colours are shown as a band so the legends read on white and on black.
- Nobody has compared the sound with real amps.

## Works Cited

<!-- works-cited: written by scripts/works-cited.py -->
::: {.works-cited}
"Ampeg SVT." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ampeg_SVT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ampeg_SVT). Bill Hughes and Roger Cox, 1969; 300 W, 14 tubes; 6146B then 6550 (mid-1970); two 8x10 cabinets; prototypes carried the Rolling Stones' 1969 US tour; blue-line / black-line faceplates.

"Fender Bassman." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fender_Bassman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fender_Bassman). 5F6 1957 three-knob tone stack, long-tailed-pair phase inverter; 5F6-A 1958 GZ34 rectifier, Presence change; four 10" Jensen P10R; copied by the Marshall JTM45; Buddy Holly.

"Fender Twin Reverb." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fender_Twin_Reverb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fender_Twin_Reverb). Blackface 1963-67, AB763, 85 W into 4 ohm, four 6L6GC, solid-state rectifier, Normal and Vibrato channels, bright switch, spring reverb (Hammond / Accutronics), "vibrato" = tremolo by a neon + LDR bug; users incl. Knopfler, Garcia, the Beatles (1968, AC568).

"Marshall Amplification." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Amplification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Amplification). JTM45 1963 after the Bassman (higher-gain ECC83s, a cap/resistor filter after the volume); 1959 Super Lead 1965, Plexiglas panel to 1969; KT66 then EL34; 4x12 stacks; inputs daisy-chained; Hendrix, Clapton, Page, Townshend.

"Mesa Boogie." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesa_Boogie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesa_Boogie). Cascading gain stages (1970s); Dual Rectifier 1991 after the Soldano SLO-100, "raw, aggressive bass-heavy sound", diamond faceplate; users incl. Korn, Tool, Soundgarden, Foo Fighters.

"Spring reverb." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_reverb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_reverb). Hammond's 1939 patent; Accutronics Type 4 / Type 8 units.

"Tone stack." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tone_stack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tone_stack). The Bassman 5F6-A standardised the three-knob tone stack; passive, it can only cut; links the Tone Stack Calculator (TSC).

"Vox AC30." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vox_AC30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vox_AC30). 1959; four EL84 cathode biased, class AB not class A, no negative feedback, GZ34; Top Boost = Bassman stack with the middle removed, standard from 1963; Celestion Blue; players Marvin, the Beatles, May (with a treble booster), the Edge.

Yeh, David T., and Julius O. Smith. "Discretization of the '59 Fender Bassman Tone Stack." *Proceedings of the 9th International Conference on Digital Audio Effects (DAFx-06)*, Montreal, 2006. [ccrma.stanford.edu/~dtyeh/papers/yeh06_dafx.pdf](https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~dtyeh/papers/yeh06_dafx.pdf). Eqn. 1: the closed-form transfer function in the Treble / Middle / Bass pot positions, checked against SPICE in the paper; bilinear discretisation (2.3); Bassman values C1 250 pF, C2 = C3 20 nF, R1 250k, R2 1M, R3 25k, R4 56k.
:::
